metadata.title: Configure Tailwind CSS v4 and Shadcn UI

story.iWant: to set up Tailwind CSS v4 and Shadcn UI components
story.soThat: I have a consistent, accessible UI framework for building the interface
story.tasks:
- Task 1: Verify Tailwind CSS v4 Installation (AC: 1) - Confirm Tailwind CSS v4 is already installed from Story 1.1 - Verify `postcss.config.mjs` contains `@tailwindcss/postcss` plugin - Check that Tailwind directives exist in `app/globals.css` - Test Tailwind utilities work in a component
- Task 2: Configure Tailwind for Monochrome Storm Theme (AC: 1) - Create/update `tailwind.config.ts` with custom theme colors - Add dark mode configuration (`darkMode: ['class']`) - Configure Inter font family - Add custom border radius values - Add glassmorphic utilities to globals.css
- Task 3: Initialize Shadcn UI (AC: 1) - Run `npx shadcn@latest init` - Configure Shadcn with TypeScript, RSC, CSS variables - Set base color to slate - Configure path aliases (@/components, @/lib/utils) - Verify `components.json` created with correct config
- Task 4: Install Required Shadcn UI Components (AC: 1) - Run `npx shadcn@latest add button` - Run `npx shadcn@latest add input` - Run `npx shadcn@latest add card` - Verify components created in `components/ui/` - Verify `lib/utils.ts` created with `cn()` helper
- Task 5: Test Styling System Integration (AC: 1) - Import Button component in `app/page.tsx` - Test Button with variants (default, outline, ghost) - Apply custom Tailwind utilities to verify theme works - Test dark mode styling - Verify no TypeScript errors in Shadcn components
- Task 6: Verify Build Process (AC: 1) - Run `npm run dev` and verify no styling errors - Run `npm run build` to ensure production build succeeds - Check that Tailwind purges unused styles correctly - Verify bundle size remains reasonable

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. **Given** the Next.js project is initialized **When** I configure the styling system **Then** Tailwind CSS v4 is installed and configured **And** Shadcn UI is initialized with the default theme **And** necessary Shadcn UI components are available (Button, Input, Card at minimum) **And** styles are applied correctly in the app **And** Tailwind utilities work in components

doc.title: Epic 1 Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Complete Tailwind config with Monochrome Storm theme: background #0a0a0a, foreground #ffffff, primary #3b82f6. Dark mode class-based, Inter font, custom border radius (16px/12px/6px).

doc.title: Epic 1 Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Shadcn config: RSC true, TypeScript, Tailwind baseColor slate, CSS variables enabled, aliases @/components and @/lib/utils.

doc.title: Architecture
doc.section: ADR-006: Shadcn UI Over Material-UI or Chakra
doc.snippet: Decision to use Shadcn UI (Radix UI + Tailwind) for copy-paste architecture, full customization, dark mode built-in, WCAG 2.1 AA accessible by default.

doc.title: UX Design Specification
doc.snippet: Base colors: Background #0a0a0a, Text #ffffff, Muted #666666, Border #222222. Semantic: Primary #3b82f6, Surface #1a1a1a, Error #ef4444, Success #10b981.

doc.title: UX Design Specification
doc.snippet: Glass card: rgba(26, 26, 26, 0.6) background, blur(20px) backdrop, 1px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1) border, 16px border-radius, 0 8px 32px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3) shadow.

doc.title: UX Design Specification
doc.snippet: Inter font family (variable weight). Type scale: h1 2.5rem/700, h2 3rem/700, h3 1.5rem/600, body 1rem/400, small 0.875rem/400.

artifact.reason: Tailwind v4 PostCSS plugin already configured from Story 1.1 - DO NOT recreate
Path aliases already configured (@/*) - Shadcn components.json must match this
Tailwind directives exist but theme needs replacement with Monochrome Storm colors and glassmorphic utilities
Currently uses Geist fonts - needs to be changed to Inter font from next/font/google
Default Next.js page - will be modified to test Button component and Tailwind utilities

story-context.constraints: - **CRITICAL**: Tailwind CSS v4 uses PostCSS plugin architecture (@tailwindcss/postcss in postcss.config.mjs), NOT traditional tailwind.config.ts - Must verify postcss.config.mjs exists from Story 1.1 before proceeding - Shadcn UI is copy-paste architecture - components copied into project, not npm installed - Dark mode MUST use class-based approach: darkMode: ['class'] - Inter font MUST be imported from next/font/google in app/layout.tsx - All custom theme colors defined in Monochrome Storm specification must be implemented - Glassmorphic utilities must be added to app/globals.css (not inline styles) - Components.json path aliases MUST match tsconfig.json (@/components, @/lib/utils) - Tailwind directives (@import "tailwindcss") must be in app/globals.css - No automated tests required for Epic 1 - validation through successful builds only

interface.name: cn() utility
interface.note: Merges Tailwind class names, resolves conflicts using tailwind-merge and clsx

interface.name: Button component
interface.note: Variants: default, outline, ghost. Sizes: default, sm, lg, icon

interface.name: Input component
interface.note: Extends HTMLInputElement, styled with glass theme

interface.name: Card components
interface.signature: Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardDescription, CardContent, CardFooter
interface.note: Composable card components for glassmorphic containers

tests.standards: No automated testing infrastructure required for Epic 1 (Foundation). Configuration validated through successful builds and manual verification. Testing standards per Tech Spec: - Configuration validated through successful builds (npm run dev, npm run build) - Manual verification: Shadcn Button component renders correctly, Tailwind utilities apply as expected, dark mode theme visible - TypeScript compilation: tsc --noEmit must pass with no errors - Production build: npm run build must complete successfully
tests.locations: No test files required for this story. Manual testing performed in: - Development server: npm run dev (verify styling applies) - Browser: localhost:3000 (visual inspection of Button, dark mode, custom theme) - Build process: npm run build (verify production build succeeds)
